# Extracellular Vesicles and CRISPR/Cas9 Delivery Systems: A Bibliometric Analysis of a Rapidly Converging Research Frontier

## Structured Abstract

**Background:** The intersection of extracellular vesicle (EV) biology and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing represents a rapidly emerging frontier in therapeutic delivery. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric mapping of the research landscape at this convergence.

**Methods:** A corpus of 259 unique publications (2015–2022) was acquired through deterministic, exhaustive retrieval and analyzed using performance indicators, science mapping, and network analysis. Bradford zoning, keyword co-occurrence, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, and co-citation networks were constructed using association-strength normalization and Louvain community detection.

**Results:** The field exhibits explosive growth with a compound annual growth rate of 66.85%, peaking at 72 publications in 2022. The citation distribution is highly skewed (mean 72.09, median 32.00), with 13.51% of works remaining uncited. The intellectual structure reveals a dominant cluster centered on EV-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 delivery for cancer therapy, supported by foundational works on exosome engineering and RNA loading strategies. The social structure is characterized by a prominent Chinese research network anchored by Xiaohui Chen (14 publications) and institutional hubs including Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University. The conceptual structure, mapped through keyword co-occurrence, identifies five thematic clusters spanning fundamental EV biology, gene editing tools, cancer applications, analytical detection methods, and therapeutic engineering.

**Conclusions:** The research domain is transitioning from foundational EV characterization toward translational applications in gene therapy, with CRISPR/Cas9 delivery emerging as the central integrating theme. The concentration of highly cited works in recent years, combined with sustained growth, suggests an accelerating trajectory toward clinical relevance.

## Introduction

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as promising biological delivery vehicles for therapeutic macromolecules, offering advantages of biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and intrinsic targeting capabilities. Concurrently, the development of CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing technology has created unprecedented opportunities for treating genetic diseases, yet its clinical translation remains constrained by delivery challenges. The convergence of these two fields represents a rapidly evolving research frontier where EVs are being engineered to encapsulate and deliver CRISPR/Cas9 components to target cells.

Understanding the structure and dynamics of this interdisciplinary domain requires systematic bibliometric analysis that moves beyond simple metric reporting toward integrated interpretation of performance, social, conceptual, and intellectual structures. This study applies established bibliometric methods [E067][E068] to map the research landscape at the intersection of extracellular vesicles and CRISPR/Cas9 delivery, examining publication trends, citation impacts, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution.

## Methods

### Data Acquisition and Corpus Construction

A systematic search was conducted to identify publications at the intersection of extracellular vesicle research and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. The retrieval process employed cursor pagination continued until the source returned no next cursor, ensuring complete acquisition [E002]. The source reported 259 results, and 259 unique source records were acquired, confirming exhaustive coverage [E002]. After deterministic exact deduplication, the final canonical corpus contained 259 unique works [E001].

### Data Quality Assessment

Metadata completeness was evaluated across all canonical works. Critical fields demonstrated high coverage: publication date, document type, title, cited-by count, reference count, and source identifier were present for 100% of records [E003]. Abstract coverage reached 84.56% (219 of 259 works), while DOI coverage was 97.3% (252 of 259 works) [E003]. Language metadata was available for 99.61% of works [E003]. These coverage rates support robust bibliometric analysis while acknowledging that abstract-level analysis cannot substitute for full-text inspection [E027–E050].

### Analytical Framework

The analytical framework followed established bibliometric guidelines [E067] and science mapping methodologies [E068][E069]. Performance analysis examined publication output, citation distributions, and productivity rankings. Science mapping employed network construction using association-strength normalization (c_ij / (w_i * w_j)) with Louvain community detection [E070] for co-authorship, institution collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, bibliographic coupling, and co-citation networks.

Network visualization parameters included maximum-spanning forest edge reduction with strongest edges per node, VOS-style community layouts for distance-based networks, and ForceAtlas2 LinLog for co-authorship networks [E022–E026]. Temporal overlay mapping was applied to keyword networks to visualize conceptual evolution [E065].

### Bradford Zoning

Source concentration was analyzed using Bradford's law, dividing ranked sources by cumulative document thirds. Records without source names were excluded from zoning [E019].

## Results

### Performance Structure: Growth, Productivity, and Impact

The research domain spans 2015 to 2022 [E004], exhibiting remarkable growth dynamics. Annual output increased from 2 publications in 2015 to 72 in 2022, representing a compound annual growth rate of 66.85% [E006][E007]. The growth trajectory shows three distinct phases: an emergence phase (2015–2017) with modest output (2–13 publications), an acceleration phase (2018–2020) where output more than doubled from 33 to 52 publications, and a consolidation phase (2021–2022) where output reached 48 and 72 publications respectively [E007]. The slight decline from 52 to 48 publications between 2020 and 2021 represents the only year-over-year decrease in the series [E007].

The corpus consists entirely of journal articles (100%), with no review or systematic review documents identified [E014]. This composition suggests a field dominated by primary research contributions rather than synthetic reviews, consistent with an emerging domain where experimental methodologies are being actively developed.

Citation impact reveals a highly skewed distribution characteristic of emerging fields. The mean citation count of 72.09 substantially exceeds the median of 32.00, indicating that a small number of highly cited works drive the average upward [E015][E017]. The 90th percentile reaches 192 citations, while the 95th percentile extends to 292.1 citations [E017]. The maximum citation count of 1,436 belongs to a 2022 publication on *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis and emerging therapeutics [E017][E018]. Notably, 35 works (13.51%) have received zero citations [E016], a proportion that must be interpreted in light of the field's recency, as 72 publications appeared in 2022 alone [E005].

The most highly cited works reveal the thematic core of the field. The top-cited publication (1,436 citations) addresses *Pseudomonas aeruginosa* pathogenesis, virulence factors, and emerging therapeutics including CRISPR-Cas systems and outer membrane vesicles [E018][E027]. The second-ranked work (651 citations) describes efficient RNA drug delivery using red blood cell extracellular vesicles, demonstrating both antisense oligonucleotide and Cas9 mRNA delivery [E018][E028]. The third-ranked publication (611 citations) presents exosome-liposome hybrid nanoparticles for CRISPR/Cas9 delivery in mesenchymal stem cells [E018][E029]. Other highly cited works address EV-based drug delivery systems considering cell source (589 citations) [E030], circular RNA targeting strategies (569 citations) [E031], and nanoparticle delivery of CRISPR/Cas9 (359 citations) [E032]. This citation hierarchy reveals that works integrating EV biology with therapeutic delivery, particularly CRISPR/Cas9 applications, dominate the impact landscape.

### Social Structure: Authors, Institutions, and Collaboration Networks

Author productivity is concentrated, with Xiaohui Chen ranking first with 14 publications—more than triple the output of the next most productive authors [E010][E011]. A cohort of nine additional researchers each contributed 4 publications: Chenghui Liu, Huilan Li, Kan Ouyang, Li Duan, Limei Xu, Shan Xing, Wei Ren, Xiao Xu, Yi He, and Yujie Liang [E011]. The co-authorship network, constructed from 131 eligible authors with minimum occurrence of 2, reveals 10 distinct collaboration clusters [E023][E060]. The network displays 149 edges among 60 displayed nodes, with the largest cluster centered on Huilan Li, Shan Xing, and Yi He (each with weighted degree 30.0), while Xiaohui Chen anchors a separate cluster with weighted degree 29.0 [E023]. The ForceAtlas2 layout achieved a layout score of 0.061 with zero overlap, indicating well-separated collaboration communities [E060].

Institutional productivity shows a tripartite leadership structure, with Harvard University, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University each contributing 7 publications [E012][E013]. Nanjing Medical University and Shaanxi Normal University follow with 5 publications each, while University of Oxford, Air Force Medical University, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Fudan University, Guangzhou Medical University, Nanjing University, National Institutes of Health, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and Shenzhen Second People's Hospital each contributed 4 publications [E013]. The institution collaboration network, constructed from 134 eligible institutions with minimum occurrence of 2, displays 10 clusters with 137 edges among 71 displayed nodes [E025][E061]. Harvard University anchors cluster 7 with weighted degree 20.0, while a dense Chinese institutional network emerges in cluster 1, connecting Guangzhou Medical University (weighted degree 18.0), Sun Yat-sen University (12.0), Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (12.0), and Fu Wai Hospital (12.0) [E025]. The VOS-style layout achieved a within-between distance ratio of 0.403, indicating moderate community separation [E061].

Source productivity is led by the *International Journal of Molecular Sciences* with 9 publications, followed by the *Journal of Extracellular Vesicles* (7 publications), *Nature Communications* and *The FASEB Journal* (6 each), and *Analytical Chemistry* and *Cancers* (5 each) [E008][E009]. Bradford zoning reveals strong source concentration: Zone 1 (the core) comprises only 23 sources yet accounts for 85 documents, while Zone 2 requires 66 sources for 87 documents, and Zone 3 disperses 85 documents across 85 sources [E019][E058]. This distribution confirms a well-defined core of journals that dominate publication output in this domain.

### Conceptual Structure: Keyword Dynamics and Thematic Clusters

Keyword temporal analysis reveals the conceptual evolution of the field. The most frequent keyword, "Biology" (235 documents), shows consistent growth from 2 documents in 2015 to 64 in 2022 [E020]. "Gene" (157 documents) follows a similar trajectory, increasing from 2 to 45 documents over the observation period [E020]. "Cell biology" (148 documents) and "Microvesicles" (123 documents) demonstrate parallel growth patterns, while "Microrna" (107 documents) and "CRISPR" (73 documents) represent more specialized but rapidly expanding themes [E020]. The keyword "CRISPR" first appears in 2016 with 1 document, grows to 10 documents by 2018, and reaches 7 documents in 2019 (the last year with complete CRISPR keyword data in the trend series) [E020].

The keyword co-occurrence network, constructed from 92 eligible keywords with minimum occurrence of 5, identifies 5 thematic clusters among 72 displayed nodes connected by 200 edges [E026][E062]. Cluster 4, anchored by "Biology" (weighted degree 2,209) and "Gene" (weighted degree 1,613), represents the fundamental biological research dimension [E026]. Cluster 2, featuring "Cell biology" (weighted degree 1,506), "Microvesicles" (weighted degree 1,412), and "Microrna" (weighted degree 1,256), captures the EV biology and RNA cargo specialization [E026]. The VOS-style layout achieved a within-between distance ratio of 0.212, indicating relatively diffuse cluster boundaries consistent with the interdisciplinary nature of the field [E062].

Temporal overlay mapping of the keyword network reveals the chronological progression of research themes, with color-encoding spanning from 2018.57 (earliest average publication year) to 2020.89 (latest) [E065]. This visualization demonstrates that newer research concentrates on applied therapeutic themes while foundational biological concepts represent earlier contributions [E065]. Density mapping further identifies areas of highest research intensity within the conceptual landscape [E066].

The three-field plot connecting leading authors, sources, and keywords reveals specific relational patterns. Xiaohui Chen's work in *Analytical Chemistry* bridges keywords including "Microvesicles," "Gene," "Biology," "Biochemistry," and "Chemistry," demonstrating the multidisciplinary nature of EV detection research [E021]. Chenghui Liu and Wei Ren similarly connect *Analytical Chemistry* with "Biochemistry," "Gene," and "Chemistry" [E021]. Pieter Vader's publications link *Cardiovascular Research* and *Nano Letters* with keywords spanning "Extracellular vesicle," "Microvesicles," "Gene," and "Cell biology" [E021]. Olivier G. de Jong's work in *Nature Communications* connects "Microvesicles," "RNA," "Microrna," "CRISPR," and "Gene" [E021]. These relational patterns illustrate how individual researchers serve as bridges between methodological domains and application areas.

### Intellectual Structure: Bibliographic Coupling and Co-Citation Networks

The bibliographic coupling network, constructed from 176 eligible documents with minimum occurrence of 5, reveals the intellectual organization of the research front. The network displays 8 clusters among 72 nodes connected by 211 edges [E022][E064]. The dominant cluster (Cluster 1) centers on gene editing by extracellular vesicles, with top nodes including "Gene Editing by Extracellular Vesicles" (weighted degree 571.0), "New Therapeutics for Extracellular Vesicles: Delivering CRISPR for Cancer Treatment" (weighted degree 418.0), and "Extracellular Vesicles as Delivery Vehicles for Therapeutic Nucleic Acids in Cancer Gene Therapy" (weighted degree 359.0) [E022]. Cluster 2 is anchored by "Prospects and challenges of extracellular vesicle-based drug delivery system: considering cell source" (weighted degree 406.0) [E022]. The VOS-style layout achieved a within-between distance ratio of 0.575, indicating well-separated intellectual communities [E064].

The co-citation network, constructed from 428 eligible cited references with minimum occurrence of 3, identifies the intellectual base of the field. The network displays 7 clusters among 72 nodes connected by 203 edges [E024][E063]. The top-cited references include works identified by OpenAlex identifiers W2793760887 (24 occurrences, weighted degree 727.0), W2754835295 (25 occurrences, weighted degree 631.0), and W2900756811 (28 occurrences, weighted degree 586.0) [E024]. The VOS-style layout achieved a within-between distance ratio of 0.389, indicating moderate intellectual base integration [E063].

## Discussion

The integrated analysis of performance, social, conceptual, and intellectual structures reveals a research domain undergoing rapid maturation from foundational discovery toward translational application. The 66.85% compound annual growth rate [E006] substantially exceeds typical growth rates in established biomedical fields, indicating sustained resource allocation and researcher entry. The concentration of output in 2022 (72 publications, representing 27.8% of the entire corpus) [E005][E007] suggests that growth has not yet plateaued, though the single year-over-year decline in 2021 [E007] warrants monitoring.

The citation distribution reveals the characteristic skew of emerging fields where a small number of pioneering works accumulate disproportionate citations. The mean-to-median ratio of 2.25 [E015] indicates that citation impact is concentrated among works that established foundational methodologies. The presence of 13.51% zero-cited works [E016] is consistent with a field where 27.8% of publications appeared in the most recent year and have had minimal time for citation accumulation [E005]. The citation window limitation is particularly relevant for interpreting impact metrics in this rapidly growing domain.

The social structure reveals a field with strong Chinese research representation, as evidenced by the institutional productivity rankings where 11 of the top 15 institutions are Chinese [E013], and the author productivity rankings where the most prolific author (Xiaohui Chen, 14 publications) [E010] and the majority of top authors are affiliated with Chinese institutions. However, the presence of Harvard University, University of Oxford, and National Institutes of Health among top institutions [E013] indicates meaningful international participation. The institution collaboration network's cluster structure [E025] suggests that collaboration remains partially organized along national lines, though cross-national linkages exist.

The conceptual structure, as revealed through keyword co-occurrence, demonstrates the field's integration of multiple disciplinary perspectives. The five thematic clusters [E026] span from fundamental biology through analytical chemistry to therapeutic engineering, reflecting the translational pipeline from basic EV characterization to clinical delivery system development. The temporal overlay [E065] indicates that CRISPR-related and therapeutic engineering themes represent more recent conceptual additions to an established foundation of EV biology research.

The intellectual structure confirms that EV-mediated CRISPR/Cas9 delivery constitutes the central integrating theme of the research front. The bibliographic coupling network's dominant cluster [E022] explicitly centers on gene editing applications, while the co-citation network [E024] reveals the intellectual foundations in both EV biology and genome editing tool development. The convergence of these previously distinct research streams represents the defining intellectual dynamic of this domain.

The Bradford distribution [E019] identifies a well-defined core of 23 journals that collectively publish one-third of all output, providing researchers with clear publication targets. The presence of both specialized EV journals (*Journal of Extracellular Vesicles*) and high-impact multidisciplinary venues (*Nature Communications*, *Science Advances*) in the core zone [E009] indicates that the field achieves visibility across the scientific community.

## Limitations

Several limitations must be acknowledged. First, citation counts are source- and retrieval-date-dependent and do not account for citation windows; recent publications have had less time to accumulate citations [E015–E017]. Second, the corpus is limited to a single source and retrieval date, and completeness is relative to the named source and query parameters [E002]. Third, network centrality measures describe corpus-specific parameterizations and do not establish causal or substantive importance [E022–E026]. Fourth, abstract-level analysis cannot support claims requiring full-text inspection [E027–E050]. Fifth, keyword frequencies depend on source metadata practices and synonym normalization [E020]. Sixth, the final publication year (2022) may be incomplete depending on retrieval timing [E005][E007]. Seventh, document-type labels inherit source classification practices [E014]. Eighth, Bradford zoning excludes records without source names [E019].

## Conclusion

This bibliometric analysis reveals a research domain at the intersection of extracellular vesicle biology and CRISPR/Cas9 delivery that is characterized by explosive growth, concentrated impact, and accelerating translational focus. The field has progressed from foundational EV characterization (2015–2017) through methodological development for cargo loading (2018–2020) toward therapeutic application in cancer and genetic diseases (2021–2022). The intellectual structure is organized around EV-mediated gene editing as the central integrating theme, supported by distinct methodological streams in EV engineering, nanoparticle hybridization, and analytical detection. The social structure features strong Chinese research networks alongside international collaboration hubs. As the field continues its rapid expansion, the transition from proof-of-concept studies toward preclinical validation and eventual clinical translation will likely define the next phase of development.
